internal.title: Kafka Consumer Lag Incident in Accounting Service
internal.body:
At 12:29 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert for high Kafka consumer lag was triggered in the accounting service. Diagnosis identified a queue backlog caused by the recent enabling of the kafkaQueueProblems flag. There was no increase in errors or latency observed. The flag was disabled at 12:49 UTC, which resolved the backlog and normalized consumer lag metrics. CPU and memory usage were normal throughout the incident.

Timeline:
- 12:29:10: Alert received for high Kafka consumer lag.
- 12:48:58: Diagnosis confirmed queue backlog linked to kafkaQueueProblems flag.
- 12:49:08: Flag disabled after approval.
- 12:49:08: Recovery verified with normalized Kafka consumer lag.

Action taken: Disabled kafkaQueueProblems flag to resolve backlog.

No resource exhaustion or other faults were detected.

external.title: Intermittent Delay in Accounting Data Processing
external.body: Between 12:29 and 12:49 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers may have experienced delays in accounting data processing due to a backlog in message consumption. The issue was identified and resolved by adjusting system settings, and normal processing resumed promptly. We continue to monitor the system to prevent recurrence.

lessons.lesson: Changes to system flags affecting Kafka consumption should be carefully monitored and rolled back promptly if they cause consumer lag without other error signals.
lessons.applies_when: When a system flag related to Kafka consumption is enabled and causes consumer lag without increased errors or latency.

action_items: Implement monitoring alerts specifically for Kafka consumer lag related to flag changes.
Establish a rollback protocol for flag changes that cause queue backlogs.
